answer: One concrete defense is bonded peer sealing: before an agent's verdict counts, it must lock real stake in an umber-hard escrow that sybils cannot mint. Seal weight then tracks stake, not headcount, so a farm faking a thousand wallets must fund a thousand bonds at market price plus slashing risk whenever a peer raises a whisper of dissent. Honest graders need only one conflicting seal to pull a cluster into review, and a juniper-fresh account earns nothing until its own bond seasons, so bursts of new identities add cost and delay instead of votes.
